name: Palmer Luckey

lean.basis: Funded the pro-Trump group Nimble America in 2016 and gave $100,000 to Trump's 2017 inauguration; a prominent Trump supporter in defense tech since.

summary: Palmer Luckey founded the virtual-reality company Oculus VR in 2012 and sold it to Facebook in 2014; he left Facebook in 2017 after controversy over his funding of a pro-Trump group, which he says got him fired and Facebook denies. He then co-founded the defense company Anduril, backed by Peter Thiel's Founders Fund and valued at $30.5 billion in 2025, and is an outspoken Trump supporter.

sources.title: Anduril raises at $30.5 billion valuation, led by Founders Fund — Fortune

connections.name: Brian Schimpf
connections.description: Co-founded Anduril in 2017 with Trae Stephens, Matt Grimm and Joe Chen; Schimpf has been CEO from the start while Luckey is the company's public face.

sources.title: Anduril's Brian Schimpf — Fortune Term Sheet

connections.name: Peter Thiel
connections.description: Thiel's Founders Fund, an early Oculus investor, seeded Anduril in 2017, led its 2018 Series A and put $1 billion, its largest-ever check, into the 2025 round that valued Anduril at $30.5 billion. Luckey met co-founder Trae Stephens at a Founders Fund retreat in 2014.

sources.title: Anduril raises at $30.5 billion valuation, led by Founders Fund — Fortune
Palmer Luckey teams with Peter Thiel for latest Anduril push forward — Orange County Business Journal

connections.name: Donald Trump
connections.description: In 2016 Luckey gave $10,000 to Nimble America, a pro-Trump group, which led to his exit from Facebook in 2017; Fortune later reported further Trump contributions. He has hosted Trump fundraisers and says he has been on "the tech-for-Trump train" longer than almost anyone.

sources.title: Oculus founder Palmer Luckey funded pro-Trump group — Fortune
Charismatic defense tech leader says Silicon Valley warming to Trump — The Washington Times

connections.name: Alex Karp
connections.description: In December 2024 Anduril and Karp's Palantir were reported to be forming a consortium with other tech firms to bid jointly for U.S. defense contracts.

sources.title: Palantir, Anduril, SpaceX and OpenAI could partner to bid for U.S. defense contracts — Fortune
Report: Palantir and Anduril join forces to try to secure U.S. government defense contracts — SiliconANGLE

connections.name: JD Vance
connections.description: Vance invested in Anduril's first venture round while at Steve Case's firm Revolution, per Bloomberg. That investment is the only documented tie; no source describes a personal relationship.

sources.title: Anduril chairman Trae Stephens on Trump and military reform — Fortune (Bloomberg)

connections.name: Mark Zuckerberg
connections.description: Facebook bought Luckey's Oculus in 2014 and he worked there until March 2017, leaving amid controversy over his pro-Trump donation (Facebook says his politics were not the reason). In May 2025 Anduril and Meta announced a partnership on military XR headsets.

sources.title: Controversial Oculus founder Palmer Luckey leaves Facebook — SiliconANGLE
Palmer Luckey and Mark Zuckerberg team up on military tech — Fortune

connections.name: Trae Stephens
connections.description: Co-founded Anduril in 2017; Stephens, a Founders Fund partner, is its executive chairman.

sources.title: Anduril business breakdown & founding story — Contrary Research

connections.name: Joe Lonsdale
connections.description: Lonsdale backed Erebor, the crypto- and defense-focused bank Luckey launched in 2025 (it won a national charter in 2025–2026), and his firm 8VC invested in Luckey's Anduril.

connections.name: Founders Fund
connections.description: An early Oculus investor; it seeded Anduril in 2017, led its 2018 Series A and put $1 billion, its largest-ever check, into the 2025 round.

connections.name: Pete Hegseth
connections.description: Hegseth toured Anduril’s Costa Mesa campus with Luckey before the December 2025 Reagan National Defense Forum and its Quonset Point, Rhode Island factory in February 2026, and in October 2026 named Luckey a co-leader of Project Meridian, the Pentagon’s future-of-warfare review.
